Seventeen comments

The Reel of Sceach

This tune was written by Joun Brady, flute player from Offaly , Ireland in the late 70s. It can be heard on the Beauties of Autumn, the LP brought out by Comhaltas in 1983 featuring the Longridge ceili band.

↳ Posted by feadog on April 25th, 2004.

the version here is not the original one!

↳ Posted by feadog on April 25th, 2004.

The Irish title is pronounced “shcahogue” according to Attracta Brady, John Brady’s daughter. The original version of the tune should be appearing in the new Portland Collection that Susan Songer will be publishing soon.

Siobhan O’Donnell’s

This tune is also the middle reel in the “Green Mountain” medley from the Dervish recording HARMONY HILL (also on LIVE IN PALMA). A very nice version, as is the one on the first Lunasa record, which tarts the tune up with some rather dramatic chord changes.

↳ Posted by Osher on June 13th, 2007.

Why don’t you post the “Black Velvet” tune yourself, if it’s not the same tune ? Siobhan has more than 1 tune associated with her name.
And to reply belatedly to “flaminfiddler”, no - “Blazin’ Fiddles” didn’t record this as “Barney’s Balmoral” - a different tune altogether, although now we’re stuck with it because some idiot has entered it as an alternative title.

Siobhan O’Donnell’s, X:10

This is a small variation on version X:1 as published here. Understandably, being in A the tune has become known in Scotland. John Brady was a flute player himself and the tune presents few problems for players of keyless flutes and whistles, only the last bar of each part having a G sharp which can be played by half covering the hole.

↳ Posted by Andrew Newland on February 13th, 2023.

Re: The Reel Of Sceachóg

I have corrected the main title of this reel that can be found on the book “The Brady Collection” compiled by Attracta and Adrian Brady.
Sceachóg means bush in irish. When deads were left after a battle in old Ireland, bushes were sown to protect them. There’s such a place near John Brady’s birthplace (from the accompanying comment in the book)
